newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Cage buys Shah's Lamborghini for $450,000.
newsitem.headline: Cage buys Shah's Lamborghini for $450,000.

text.p: Hollywood actor Nicolas Cage on Wednesday bought the star of a sale of 10 exotic sports cars that the late Shah of Iran once rode around Swiss and Iranian mountain roads, auctioneers Brooks Europe said.

Cage bought the red Lamborghini Miura SVJ, for a whopping 660,000 Swiss Francs ($450,000), bidding by telephone at the auction, which had provided a vivid reminder of the Shah's enormous wealth and excess.
The Lamborghini was built to Muhammad Reza Pahlavi's special order and secretly delivered to his St Moritz chalet for a ski holiday before Christmas 1971.

With fewer than 3,000 km on the clock and with its original studded snow tyres for skiing trips, it was first flown to the Iranian Embassy in Rome, checked by the Shah's guards for bombs and bugs and then taken to Switzerland.
The Hollywood actor, who won an Oscar last year for his role in "Leaving Las Vegas," has a passion for cars and is reported to already own another Lamborghini, a Rolls-Royce and a Porsche.
"This is crazy. This price is too high. It seems the heat is back on the market," said Waldemar Glasman, a German dealer on the depressed market for classic and vintage cars.

Most of the cars, owned by the Shah, then known as the King of Kings, at the height of his powers and stored carefully since Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution, had not been seen in public since he himself last drove them.
They were only a tiny fraction of his staggering collection of some 3,000 cars, including more than 2,000 Mercedes Benz saloons and Range Rovers.
Ironically, the sale had the feel of a second-hand car sales pitch. "Low mileage, good condition, usability, affordability," said a leaflet distributed at the auction.
The cars, along with other riches including jewellery, art, treasures and planes, were left behind when the Shah fled Iran in January 1979 at the controls of his Boeing 707.

After he died of cancer in Egypt in July 1980, 10 low-mileage cars including a selection of Rolls-Royces, a Cadillac, a Daimler and a metallic green 1974 Ferrari presented by Jordan's King Hussein were hidden in a warehouse.
About five years ago, they were sold in one lot to a secretive collector from the United Arab Emirates.

Legend has it that the Shah drove his sports cars at over 200 km per hour through Iran's narrow, winding mountain roads or around Swiss ski resorts. Empress Farah was so scared that she had to close her eyes, according to one book about the family.
In Tehran, all of the expensive cars were kept on standby with full petrol tanks. When they needed servicing, they would be loaded onto the royal plane and returned to manufacturers.
But in Geneva on Wednesday, some of them were bargains.
A primrose yellow 1968 Lamborghini Espada, in which the Shah used to drive his crown prince son to school, made 42,000 Swiss francs ($23,000), way below its estimated price.

The Shah's summer car, a 1973 Aston Martin V8, originally kept at his holiday palace on the shores of the Caspian Sea, was also sold for 42,000 Swiss francs while a 1973 Daimler limousine fetched 23,000 Swiss Francs ($15,600).
Few Middle Eastern buyers joined the auction, although a Saudi man wearing a million-dollar diamond-studded watch bought a Rolls Royce Camargue for 80,000 Swiss Francs ($55,000).
Asked if he would be driving the car himself, an aide said: "No. We have a driver."
